court: Lehigh County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Dispute over borough building-line ordinance, street widening, and eminent domain compensation; no compensated occupancy of a dwelling/rooms or its regulation is at issue.

Elderly relative occupied a house her nephew purchased out of family kindness; court found no implied contract to pay rent. Not a lodger/boarder arrangement, letting for pay, or regulation of letting; purely an intra-family gratuitous occupancy dispute over an estate claim.

court: Montgomery County Court of Common Pleas
holding_summary: Where a deed restricted use of the premises to 'private residence,' the court declared that erecting and using an apartment-house — a structure operated for profit and occupied by numerous rent-paying tenant families — would violate the restriction, because an apartment-house (even one excluding transient hotel guests) is not itself a 'private residence.'

quotes.text: The structure contemplated is, as we understand it, an ordinary one of this character to be operated for profit, or as a business enterprise, and intended to be occupied by a large number of tenants, each of whom will rent a suite of apartments therein for use by himself and family for private residence.
An apartment-house is not a private residence, nor is the occupant of such in private residence.

we, therefore, declare and advise, as a declaratory judgment or decree, that, in our opinion, the restriction in petitioner’s deed prohibits use of any structure hereafter erected on his premises as an apartment-house.

notes: No occupancy had actually occurred (declaratory judgment on a proposed, unbuilt structure), so duration_of_occupancy is unclear; the case is doctrinally adverse in that it treats a commercial, rent-collecting multi-tenant letting arrangement as categorically distinct from, and incompatible with, private residential use, even though enforced via private covenant rather than police-power regulation.
Concerns validity of a borough ordinance restricting bill-boards on private property; no bearing on compensated occupancy of dwellings/rooms or lodging regulation.

court: Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Dispute over a restaurant occupant's right to a stall/space in a city-owned market-house; occupancy is of commercial market space, not a dwelling or rooms, so it does not bear on residential letting or its regulation despite discussing license-vs-tenancy status.

court: Butler County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Landlord-tenant covenant dispute over an entire hotel property being handed over wholesale by the lessee to an employee (breach of covenant against subletting) and a penalty-vs-liquidated-damages question; concerns transfer of an entire commercial hotel business between operators, not compensated occupancy of rooms by lodgers/boarders or its regulation.

court: Philadelphia County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Routine apartment-house landlord-tenant dispute over the landlord's covenant to enforce quiet-enjoyment rules against a noisy neighboring tenant, resulting in constructive eviction; does not address the legal character of letting or its regulation, only breach of a quiet-enjoyment covenant.
Ground-rent extinguishment and estoppel case; no compensated dwelling occupancy or letting-regulation issue.

Public Service Commission rate-regulation dispute between a bridge company and a street-railway company over lease rental for track space on a bridge; wholly a utility-ratemaking matter, not residential letting.
Mineral/timber reservation deed-construction case; no dwelling occupancy or letting issue.

Building-restriction case about whether a new multi-story porch violates a deed covenant on setback lines; concerns architectural covenant enforcement, not compensated occupancy or letting of rooms/dwellings.
Mining-subsidence/water-supply damages case; no letting or occupancy-for-pay issue.

Building-restriction case enjoining construction of a theatre in violation of a 'dwelling houses only' covenant; concerns building type/use classification for a theatre, not compensated occupancy of rooms/dwellings by lodgers or boarders.

Affidavit-of-defense sufficiency question in an assumpsit action; the underlying facts involve a wife's continued occupancy of her family's former home after mortgage foreclosure, with a set-off claim for reasonable use-and-occupation value — not a householder letting rooms/dwellings to lodgers or boarding-house regulation.
Partition/ejectment dispute among cotenant heirs turning on estoppel and adverse possession; mesne-profits figure is incidental to a title dispute, not a letting or lodging arrangement.
Borough hawker/peddler licensing ordinance applied to door-to-door meat sales; regulates itinerant selling of goods, not lodging/boarding of occupants.
Replevin action over a landlord's illegal distress (picking a lock to seize a tenant's goods); a distress-procedure case, not about the legal character of letting or its regulation.

Wrongful-distress damages action under the Act of 1772 for seizure of a tenant's horse when no rent was actually due; a distress/damages procedure dispute unrelated to letting characterization or its regulation.
